# Function version compatibility

<!-- Generated by tools/version_compatibility.py; do not edit by hand. -->

This catalog separates the released sources to which each existing mathematical
contract applies from the exact Rust function bindings already registered in this checkout.
Neither source review nor passing finite tests establish a Rust implementation proof.

## Select a model for a resolved build

Every one of the 599 registered model entries has an applicability record.
The lookup distinguishes exact reviewed releases from explicitly declared compatible ranges.
Compatible ranges assume preservation of the modeled behavior, including relevant dependency
operations and implementation-specific results; SemVer is evidence for that assumption, not a proof.
Ranges stay within one Cargo compatibility line, retain the registry origin and exclude prereleases.
Exact git revisions and profiles without a compatible range remain exact. No contract is weakened.
Target, feature and dependency filters appear only where the source review records a behavior difference.
Missing facts required by a profile produce `unresolved`; a known mismatch produces `unsupported`.

```bash
python3 tools/lookup_applicability.py --build build.json
```

Run from this package directory. Use `--model <registered-model-id>` to select one operation.
A checkout reads the current source registry; an exported manifest also supports standalone lookup.
It returns model, contract and catalog names, matching source item mappings, reasons for
rejection and the existing interpretation conditions. See [the build and result schema](BINDINGS.md#selecting-a-reviewed-build).

In Lean, `catalog.forBuild build` preserves the same keys, families, indices, roles and
mathematical specifications, while selecting matching source-call identities at the actual release.
Members without an existing source-call registration remain mathematical capabilities and
receive no callable identity. The six source-less helpers inherit applicability through named consumers.

The [curated source registry](source-map.json) records immutable archive checksums,
exact git revisions and per-function source arguments. `just generate-specs` exports the machine-readable
`applicability.json`; it is not committed. Neither matching nor source review supplies a Rust implementation proof.

The shared interpretation boundary is:

- Custom-allocator failure while constructing an error or diagnostic payload is outside the scope of this package; interpret those allocations as successful. Other errors, panics, ordinary allocation effects and callback outcomes retain their model contracts.
- Applicability selects an existing mathematical model under its recorded conditions. It does not prove Rust implementation correctness or discharge generic-index, ownership, codec, provider or runtime interpretation obligations.
- Declared compatible ranges assume that the registered operation and its relevant dependencies preserve the complete reference contract, at the used types and recorded build conditions, including implementation-specific diagnostics, effects and source identities. Reference releases and test lockfiles are evidence, not an exhaustive eligibility list. Known behavioral exceptions remain excluded; no Cargo resolution or Rust correspondence proof is inferred.

## Function applicability

Each profile is an alternative; all filters within that profile must hold.
Renamed predecessor items are listed explicitly. The lookup prints the full interpretation
conditions and source arguments for each alternative, including resolved dependency origins.

### token-extension-type-list

Reviewed 2026-11-09; crate `spl-token-2022-interface`.

Registered releases: `3.1.1`.

Published releases in the review window: `0.0.0`, `1.0.0`, `2.0.0`, `2.1.0`, `3.0.0`, `3.0.1`, `3.1.0`, `3.1.1`, `3.1.2`, `4.0.0`.

This section records the existing exact bindings. Current source applicability is selected by the per-function profiles above and their immutable source reviews.

| Version | Public contract | Pinned source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 3.1.1 | `Solanalib.Specs.SplToken2022Interface.extension.BaseStateWithExtensions.get_extension_types_operational_contract` | [src/extension/mod.rs](https://github.com/solana-program/token-2022/blob/e18f9c6f9bf6044b934f48e3090e8e59e4820f02/interface/src/extension/mod.rs) |

**Behavior differs in 2.1.0:** With a complete TLV entry whose type tag is 28 and whose payload fits, 2.1.0 returns InvalidAccountData because that enum variant does not exist. Version 3.1.1 recognizes PermissionedBurn and can return it in the list. The unrestricted 3.1.1 type-list model therefore cannot be reused for 2.1.0. The older scan also pushes the type before checking that its value fits, whereas 3.1.0 and later check the value bounds first; the full contract preserves this difference in allocation and abnormal-exit order. ([source](https://github.com/solana-program/token-2022/blob/4fae3ba6516db0c6e4b2fe698ba2cfdb92901b93/interface/src/extension/mod.rs#L1135)).
